# Syrtis v1.4.1

**Cursor usage syncs for accounts moved to Cursor's new billing, and Gemini models appear under one name.** Both changes come from the macOS app (Syrtis 2.11.2 and 2.11.3).

## Fixes

- **Cursor usage syncs again for accounts moved to Cursor's new billing.** ([#279](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/279)) Thanks [@ohari5336](https://github.com/ohari5336), who reported the failure in [syrtis#520](https://github.com/Nanako0129/syrtis/issues/520) and ran the checks that shaped the fix.

  For these accounts cursor.com answers the usage request Syrtis has always used with a success status but no list of usage events, so Syrtis synced nothing for them. Syrtis still asks the old endpoint first on every sync. Only when it answers that way does Syrtis read usage from Cursor's `v2/query-billing-items` endpoint instead. An account the old endpoint still serves is handled as before.

  Three things change for an account read this way:

  - Usage from before the switch stays. At the first successful read from the new endpoint, Syrtis keeps the rows it already had in a separate file next to the usage file and takes only the new endpoint's rows dated after the newest of them. If a later sync is answered by the old endpoint again, that file is deleted.
  - Sessions are counted per day, because the new endpoint carries no conversation id.
  - A row Cursor reports with a charge of 0 (plan-included usage) is priced from Syrtis's own price table; a row with a positive USD charge keeps Cursor's amount, rounded to the cent. Only rows of the Cursor product are read.

  Each usage item has to belong to the user in your Cursor sign-in, or to one other user id that Cursor marks as a user, the same for the whole sync. Anything else stops the sync and nothing is saved. This path adds four lines that the Cursor line in Settings > Accounts can show, each ending in its code: "Cursor's new billing asks for a team for this account, which Syrtis can't read yet (billing_v2_team_required).", "Cursor's new billing didn't provide this account's usage (billing_v2_unavailable). Syrtis will try again later.", "Cursor's new billing has no usage for this account yet (billing_v2_no_items). Syrtis will try again later." or "Cursor returned usage of another account, so Syrtis saved nothing (billing_v2_principal_mismatch)."

  This has not run against an account that is actually on the new billing; the new endpoint was tested against a local stand-in server. On the maintainer's Windows test PC, an account still on the old billing synced as before ("Last synced", no permission prompt), and no extra history file appeared.

- **Gemini models appear under one name, and one row per model and provider when several apps are selected.** ([#278](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/278))

  The Models list showed `gemini-4-argon-c` and `gemini-4-argon-trial` beside `gemini-4-argon`, and the `gemini-3.5-flash` tiers (high, medium, low, extra-low) beside `gemini-3.5-flash`. They are now shown under the bare model name. Only the displayed name changes: prices, the usage cache and exports keep the original label, and nothing is read again.

  When the selection covers more than one app (Overview, or the Antigravity tab with both the CLI and the extension), a model from one provider is now one row, and hovering over it lists each app's tokens and share. A row whose cost is flagged as implausible is never merged with others. The Overview Models card and "Favorite model" in Stats use the same rows.

  On the test PC, the Antigravity tab showed `gemini-3.8-flash` once and none of the suffixed names, and on Overview `gpt-6-astra` was one row whose tooltip listed Codex 95% and Claude 5%.
